data.body:
SECOND, DISTINCT py3.11 FAILURE MODE ON THE SAME CELL — recorded here because this ticket is the natural home for 'the ubuntu-latest/py3.11 cell is unstable', even though the specific HANG it was filed for is fixed.

Observed 2026-08-07 on Gerrit change 1520 (ticket e6e9), patch set 1, TWICE:

  test_opcert_service_app.py::test_matching_guard_is_accepted - worker 'gw3' crashed

ubuntu/py3.11 ONLY. 11,316 tests passed on each run; the reported 'Coverage failure: total of 15' was downstream of the dead worker, not an independent failure.

This is a CRASH, not the 99%-silent-until-timeout HANG this ticket describes — a different signature on the same matrix cell.

The investigating agent did NOT treat it as a flake on faith, and ruled out the obvious explanations:
* the file is the opcert FastAPI service, UNTOUCHED by that change;
* it passes locally in 0.88s under CI's exact `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` guard, so it was not a timeout;
* a local full-suite run under CI's exact `-n 4 --dist worksteal` config produced no crash;
* the IDENTICAL patch set, rebased with no content change, then passed py3.11 in 11m42s.

So: not attributable to the change, not reproducible locally, and it cleared on a content-free rebase — i.e. environment- or runner-specific to that cell, same as the hang.

Why it is worth keeping together: two DIFFERENT failure modes now attach to ubuntu/py3.11 specifically, both non-reproducible locally, both costing full CI cycles on unrelated changes in a saturated queue, and both initially reading as a rejection of an innocent change. If a third appears, the useful question stops being 'what is wrong with this test' and becomes 'why is this matrix cell unreliable' — worth deciding whether py3.11 stays in the gating matrix or moves to an advisory lane.

Not reopening this ticket, since the hang it names is genuinely fixed. Filed as a comment so the pattern stays discoverable from the ticket that owns the cell.
